summary: Algeria requires a consular visa obtained in advance for nearly every nationality — only a handful of Maghreb states plus a few others are exempt. The main exception is the Saharan tourism scheme, under which groups of tourists on trips organised by approved travel agencies can be issued a visa on arrival for the far-southern wilayas.

Only travelers with residency status may bring in or take out Algerian dinar banknotes, up to DZD 10,000.

notes: Canada's travel advice says you must declare all foreign currency on arrival and report each exchange during your stay, and show the declaration form and bank exchange receipts when you leave. Algerian dinars cannot be taken out of the country.
The UK FCDO says it is illegal to bring drones, binoculars, telescopes and certain types of photography equipment into Algeria without authorisation; check with Algerian customs before you travel.
Canada's travel advice says to carry a copy of your prescriptions and keep medication in its original container.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice describes Algeria as a cash-based economy: credit cards are usually accepted at major hotels but rarely in restaurants and other businesses, and ATMs that take foreign cards — in banks and a few major hotels — are unreliable. It also says exchanging currency on the black market is illegal.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel within 30 km of Algeria's borders with Libya, Mauritania, Mali and Niger and parts of the Tunisian border, and against all but essential travel near the rest of the border with Tunisia.

tips.text: Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists on trips organised by approved travel agencies to the great South can be issued a visa on arrival valid for up to 30 days. The measure applies only to the wilayas of Tamanrasset, Illizi, Tindouf, Adrar, Béchar, Timimoun, Djanet, Bordj Badji Mokhtar, Béni Abbès, In Salah and Touggourt.
For a tourist visa, Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs asks for an accommodation certificate (certificat d'hébergement), a hotel booking or a travel-agency certificate.

Canada's travel advice says cards are rarely accepted outside major hotels, that exchanging currency on the black market is illegal, that you must show bank receipts for all exchanges when you leave, and that dinars cannot be taken out of the country.

Australia's Smartraveller advises against all travel within 450 km of the borders with Mali and Niger and within 100 km of the borders with Mauritania, Libya and Tunisia because of terrorism and kidnapping.

Canada's travel advice says photographing sensitive installations, including military sites, government buildings and bridges, is prohibited, and Australia's Smartraveller says photographing sensitive sites, government and military buildings or security personnel is illegal.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Algeria?
faq.answer: Yes, for most nationalities. Algeria's embassy in Helsinki says all non-Algerians need a visa by default and names the exceptions for ordinary passports: Libya, Mauritania, Tunisia, Malaysia, the Maldives, Mali and Seychelles (it also lists Morocco, but Algeria reinstated the visa for Moroccan passport holders on 26 September 2024). Everyone else must obtain a visa from an Algerian consulate before travel, unless entering under the Saharan tour visa-on-arrival scheme.

faq.question: Does Algeria have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says foreigners must obtain a visa in advance from diplomatic and consular posts; no official source we could read describes an eVisa. On arrival, a visa can be issued under the Saharan tourism scheme to groups on organised tours to the far south; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also says a regularization visa may be issued on arrival exceptionally, in an emergency.

faq.question: Can I get an Algerian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Only under the Saharan tourism scheme: Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists on trips organised by approved travel agencies to the great South (wilayas such as Djanet or Tamanrasset) can be issued a visa on arrival valid for up to 30 days. It applies only to the listed southern wilayas.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Algeria?
faq.answer: Rarely. Canada's travel advice says credit cards are usually accepted at major hotels but rarely in restaurants and other businesses, and that ATMs taking foreign cards are unreliable. It also says you must keep bank receipts for every exchange and that dinars cannot be taken out of the country.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Algeria?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states Algeria's entry rule for Israeli passport holders.
